text:
The impact of this data breach is severe due to the highly sensitive nature of the compromised information. The unauthorized access included not only personal identifiers like patient names but also critical health data such as medical histories and treatment information, alongside financial data like health insurance details.

This combination of protected health information (PHI) and personally identifiable information (PII) significantly elevates the risk for the 200,000 affected individuals. Specifically, the exposure of insurance details and medical histories creates a direct pathway for identity theft and insurance fraud. Unlike a breach involving only non-sensitive data, this incident poses long-term financial and privacy risks, as medical records are often targeted by criminals for fraudulent billing or selling on the dark web, while the personal data facilitates broader identity theft schemes.
